- When sentiment is positive (1.00) in the last 1–2 days, model tends to overreact — inflate prices, especially in early forecast days; reduce early forecast peaks by 2–5%.
- Model consistently overestimates 30-day price peaks (especially 10–15 day horizon) after recent spikes; apply downward bias of 1–3% to forecasted peaks.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) for 10+ days, model overestimates mean price; adjust forecast mean downward by 0.5–1.5% to align with recent 18-day average.
- Model underestimates price drops after spikes — especially in 10–15 day horizon; if sentiment turns negative, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- Forecasting horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher prices; apply 1–2% downward correction to 30d forecast if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is positive and model forecasts a spike, reduce the peak by 2–4% and shift the peak forward by 1–2 days to avoid overshoot.
- Model tends to overestimate 10–15 day price movements after 18-day neutral sentiment; apply 1–2% downward correction to those horizons.
